tax.text: She said taxes should fully fund public schools and teachers.
tax.quote: Taxes should fully fund public schools and public school teachers.

wages.text: She said she wants to raise the minimum wage to at least $15 an hour in South Carolina.
wages.quote: I would like to raise the minimum wage to at least $15/hour in SC.

trade.text: Her campaign calls for reducing tariffs to ease costs for families.
trade.quote: Rein in tariffs and unnecessary foreign conflicts, easing the burden they impose on families like yours

debt.text: Her campaign says she would restore funding to Medicare and expand Medicare eligibility.
debt.quote: Restore funding to Medicare, Medicaid, and the Affordable Care Act.

housing.text: Her housing plan includes funding projects that build housing near jobs and transit.
housing.quote: Fund smart-growth projects that build housing near jobs and public transportation while incorporating child care centers.

schools.text: She opposes vouchers and supports more funding for public schools and teachers.
schools.quote: Trust teachers and librarians to make decisions for schools and libraries; oppose vouchers; increase salaries for teachers and funding for public schools and public libraries; increase federal money going to Title 1 schools.

safety.text: She favors keeping police funding at its current level while adding taxpayer-supported community programs to prevent crime.
safety.quote: I prefer not to take any existing funding from police departments. Rather I would like to keep police funding at the current level and add tax payer supported community programs that help prevent crime.

immigration.text: She supports civil-rights protections and due process for immigrants.
immigration.quote: Pass laws to protect everyone’s civil rights and return due process also for immigrants.

guns.text: She supports background checks on all gun purchases, safe-storage requirements, and an age limit of 21 for gun ownership.
guns.quote: I support background checks on all gun purchases regardless of where they are purchased. I support laws that require guns to be locked when not in use, especially in homes with children.

abortion.text: She said women should make the decision about abortion for their families.
abortion.quote: I trust women to make the best decision for their family.

gender.text: She said transgender women should be treated as women and transgender men as men.
gender.quote: Transgender women are women and should be allowed to do what women do. Transgender men should be allowed to do what men do.

health.text: Her campaign supports restoring public health-program funding and lowering the Medicare eligibility age.
health.quote: Lower the enrollment age for Medicare to 64 next year.

energy.text: She called for expanding green-energy funding, speeding solar and wind permitting, and restoring EPA standards.
energy.quote: Restore and expand funding for green energy projects for homes, governments and businesses; Permitting reform to allow solar and wind projects to be completed quicker; restore EPA standards.

voting.text: She supports voting-rights legislation and opposes the SAVE Act.
voting.quote: Pass the John Lewis Voting Rights Advancement Act and other acts that support voting rights. Oppose the SAVE act.

debt.text: Her campaign describes excessive spending and debt as harmful to future generations and says she will fight for fiscal responsibility.
debt.quote: As our next Congresswoman, Sheri will fight for fiscal responsibility, accountability, and transparency of our hard-earned tax dollars.

schools.text: She voted for H.R. 1, which created a federal tax credit for contributions to scholarship-granting organizations.
schools.quote: Congresswoman Sheri Biggs (R-SC-03) today voted to pass H.R. 1, the One Big Beautiful Bill Act.

immigration.text: Her campaign says she will build the wall, stop illegal immigration and replace catch-and-release with stop-and-deport.
immigration.quote: As our next Member of Congress, Sheri will work tirelessly to build the wall, stop the flow of illegal aliens and drugs into our country, and replace “catch-and-release” with “stop-and-deport.”

guns.text: She introduced bills to remove federal firearm mailing and short-barreled-shotgun restrictions.
guns.quote: Law-abiding citizens will no longer have to pay a $200 tax or complete months-long paperwork just to own a practical firearm for self-defense.

abortion.text: Her campaign says she will use her voice to protect the sanctity of life and advance a culture of life.
abortion.quote: AS our Member of Congress, Sheri will use her voice and story to protect the sanctity of life and advance a true culture of life in this country.

gender.toward: rules based on sex at birth
gender.text: She voted for the Protection of Women and Girls in Sports Act, which bases Title IX athletic eligibility on reproductive biology and genetics at birth.
gender.quote: Protection of Women and Girls in Sports Act

health.text: Her official health-policy page identifies competition and flexibility as policy cornerstones.
health.quote: Competition, flexibility, transparency, and an emphasis on rural communities must remain cornerstones of proposed policy initiatives.

trade.text: He argues that protective tariffs distort markets and limit consumer choice.
trade.quote: Brian maintains that you cannot support a “pro-market” position while endorsing protective tariffs or state interference in trade, as this distorts markets and limits consumer choice.

debt.text: He says he consistently criticizes spending and budget practices that increase debt.
debt.quote: Yes — he consistently criticizes wasteful spending, unsustainable budget practices, and policies that increase debt without corresponding value to citizens.

health.text: He opposes expanding government in health care and favors market-oriented reforms and competition.
health.quote: Brian believes the current healthcare system is hampered by both parties’ plans that rely on government centralization. He advocates for market-oriented reforms that expand choice, reduce regulatory barriers, and let competition lower costs.
